title: Personal LLM inference mini-sheet
content:
Experiment tracker - quick mini-sheet

Columns: ExpID | Date | Model | Quant | Batch | Seq | Tokens/s | P50(ms) | P95(ms) | Cost/1k | Notes

EXP-001 | 2025-10-28 | redwood-rlhf-7B | int8 | 8 | 512 | 12,400 | 42 | 120 | $0.45 | baseline; kernel opt A
EXP-002 | 2025-10-30 | ggml-13B | q4_0 | 4 | 2048 | 9,100 | 85 | 210 | $0.62 | long context slow; try KV cache
EXP-003 | 2025-11-03 | redwood-rlhf-7B | int8 | 16 | 256 | 18,900 | 35 | 90 | $0.38 | good throughput w/ batching
EXP-004 | 2025-11-08 | instruction-13B | int8+ | 8 | 1024 | 10,500 | 60 | 140 | $0.51 | P95 noisy under burst

Notes to self:
- For experiments with high P95, re-run with jittered arrival and measure tail latency per-host.
- Add KV-prefetch for seq>1024 cases (see GitHub PR #867).
- Cost calc: token price based on reserved capacity price model; verify with billing-estimate script.

Actions / Next steps:
- Re-run EXP-002 with KV cache + autotune kernel selector (target window 1024-2048).
- Compare int8 vs int8+ on 7B with batch sizes 8/16 for latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Create small dashboard in Console (quick chart: tokens/s vs p95) and link in Confluence.

Quick references:
- Slack: #eng-applied-ml thread 'perf-mini-bench'
- Confluence: /inference/perf-benchmarks-2025
- JIRA: PERF-1423 (investigate kernel selection)

Scratch / raw notes:
- observed CPU spike on host-a when batch=16 for 7B — maybe host hitting memcpy bottleneck
- testing with 2 micro-batches of 8 improved p95 by ~12ms
- TODO: add column 'env' (dedicated vs hosted)
